parsed.summary: The Lean file states, with the proofs left as `sorry`, that there exist finitely generated ICC Kazhdan property-(T) groups Γ and Λ with isomorphic group von Neumann algebras (as trace-preserving, normal *-isomorphisms) but non-isomorphic as groups. It also states the infinite version: Λ together with a sequence Γₙ of pairwise non-isomorphic such groups, all with the same group factor. The definitions (ICC, property (T), L(G), the trace) look faithful. The main gap is that the 'index 24ⁿ subgroup / commensurable' clause of Theorem 1.2 is not formalized.

glossary.plain: A bundled group whose carrier type (in universe u) is countable.
G is infinite and every non-identity element has an infinite conjugacy class.
There is a multiplicative equivalence G ≃* H.
Every unitary representation on a complex Hilbert space (in Type u) with almost invariant unit vectors (for every finite K and ε>0) has a nonzero invariant vector.
glossary.standard_concept: Kazhdan property (T) for a discrete group
glossary.note: The Hilbert space is restricted to Type u (here Type 0). This is harmless for countable groups. The group is discrete, so no continuity is needed.

glossary.plain: The left regular representation of G on ℓ²(G), (λ_g f)(h) = f(g⁻¹h).
The double commutant S'' of a set S of operators, packaged as a von Neumann algebra.
glossary.standard_concept: von Neumann algebra generated by S
glossary.note: The centralizer is taken in the star-algebra sense. The generating set here is star-closed, so this is fine.

glossary.plain: L(G), the double commutant of {λ_g} in B(ℓ²(G)).
A *-isomorphism that preserves suprema of families of projections in both directions.
glossary.note: Supremum is taken within the algebra via the order p*q = p. This is the standard order-theoretic characterization of normality.

glossary.plain: A normal, trace-preserving *-algebra isomorphism L(G) ≅ L(H).
glossary.standard_concept: isomorphism of von Neumann algebras L(G) ≅ L(H)
glossary.note: For ICC groups the trace is unique, so the trace-preservation and normality requirements are automatic. This is equivalent to abstract isomorphism, not stronger in substance.

glossary.plain: There exists a TracialGroupFactorEquiv between L(G) and L(H).

lean_claims.plain: There exist countable groups Γ, Λ (in Type 0), both finitely generated, ICC and with property (T), such that L(Γ) ≅ L(Λ) via a normal trace-preserving *-isomorphism, but Γ ≇ Λ as groups.

There exist a countable group Λ and a sequence Γₙ of countable groups, all finitely generated, ICC and with property (T), such that L(Γₙ) ≅ L(Λ) for all n, L(Γₘ) ≅ L(Γₙ) for all m, n, Γₘ ≇ Γₙ for m ≠ n, and Λ ≇ Γₙ for all n.

paper_claims.plain: There exist finitely generated ICC property-(T) groups Λ, Γ₀, Γ₁, … that are pairwise non-isomorphic with L(Γₙ) ≅ L(Λ) for n ≥ 0. Moreover Γₙ contains a subgroup isomorphic to Γ₀ of index 24ⁿ (so the Γₙ are mutually commensurable).
The pair Λ, Γ₀ disproves Connes's conjecture: ICC property-(T) groups with isomorphic group factors that are non-isomorphic.

coverage.why: Lean has the existence, f.g., ICC, (T), factor isomorphism and pairwise non-isomorphism (including Λ vs Γₙ). It omits the 'Moreover' clause about index-24ⁿ subgroups and commensurability.
Counterexample to Connes's conjecture with the extra finitely-generated conclusion. The statement is faithful assuming the definitions are right.
No statement about subgroups or index.

flags.explanation: The paper's 'Moreover' part (each Γₙ contains a subgroup isomorphic to Γ₀ of index 24ⁿ, hence mutual commensurability) is absent from the Lean statement. The Lean theorem is therefore weaker than the full Theorem 1.2. The excerpt's '24n' is presumably 24ⁿ, but this is garbled in the excerpt.
flags.probe_idea: Add to the existential: ∀ n, ∃ H : Subgroup (Γ n), H.index = 24^n ∧ Nonempty (H ≃* Γ 0), and check that it is consistent with the existing conjuncts.

flags.explanation: The paper writes L(Γ) ≅ L(Λ) (abstract von Neumann algebra isomorphism). Lean requires a normal, trace-preserving *-isomorphism of the concrete double commutants. For ICC groups these are equivalent because the trace is unique and *-isomorphisms of von Neumann algebras are automatically normal. In a positive existential this makes Lean's conclusion nominally stronger and harmless.

Property (T) quantifies only over Hilbert spaces in Type u, with u = 0 in the theorems. Since the groups are countable, this is equivalent to the full definition. Quantifying over a smaller class makes property (T) a priori weaker as a conclusion, but not in substance.

Positivity side condition inside a proof term for ℓ² membership.
Rewriting the ℓ² norm via the p = 2 tsum formula inside the isometry proof.
Same: part of the norm-preservation proof.
